accuracy.evidence: Data checked against standard A-level data tables (CRC Handbook values): butane −0.5 °C, propanal 48 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C at Mr 58/58/60; pentane 36 °C, butanal 75 °C, butan-1-ol 118 °C at Mr 72/72/74; propane −42 °C, ethanal 20 °C, ethanol 78 °C; aldehyde series methanal −19, ethanal 20, propanal 48, butanal 75, pentanal 103, hexanal 131 °C; solubility propanal ≈31, butanal ≈7, pentanal ≈1.2, hexanal ≈0.6 g per 100 mL with ethanal miscible. Mr = 14n + 16 and electrons = 8n + 8 for CnH2nO verified for n = 1 to 8.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented AQA and OCR examiner-report slips: aldehydes hydrogen bonding to themselves because they contain O (forces step prediction, challenge tag self), boiling breaking the C=O covalent bond (tags cov and brk, mastery m5), Mr as the reason the alcohol boils higher (tag mr, m6), water's H bonding to the δ+ carbonyl carbon (water-step target with like-charge feedback, p3), and longer chains dissolving less because of weaker London forces (tag weak, m3).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcbp is about bulk properties of carbonyls specifically: ranking matched-Mr triples alkane, carbonyl, alcohol; picking the force set for propanal and propanone; drawing water's δ+ H onto the carbonyl oxygen's lone pair; sliding the C1 to C6 aldehyde series with paired boiling point and solubility bars; and pinning Mr 44/46 compounds on a thermometer. flagimf covers hydride trends and alkane branching, and flagcarb covers naming and nucleophile attack. The 30% shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step reveals the rule by doing: rung order shows each boiling point only once placed, the forces step names why propanal has no hydrogen bonds between its own molecules, the water step rejects the δ+ carbon with 'Like charges repel', and the chain slider makes learners find butanal as the first below 10 g per 100 mL and pentanal as the first above 100 °C, so the opposing trends are seen, not told.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'No: same Mr, same forces' for propanal versus butane, 'Yes: they contain oxygen' for propanal self hydrogen bonding, and 'rises: stronger London forces' for solubility with chain length. Each following task makes the learner act against the wrong pick, and A.reveal quotes the guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions, each with two tagged distractors and specific corrections: self (no H on O so no hydrogen bonds between carbonyl molecules), cov and brk (boiling overcomes forces between molecules, not C=O), mr (Mr 60 vs 58 is almost the same), nodip, ion (propanone stays molecular and accepts hydrogen bonds), noco and weak (hexanal has stronger London forces; the chain is the problem). Streak counter and Another button.

readability.evidence: Learner kid text stays under the learner kid limit of 6.5 with short sentences and concrete numbers (propanal boils at 48 °C, butane at about 0 °C). Adult text stays under 9.5 while using the exact specification terms permanent dipole–dipole forces, London forces, hydrogen bonds, lone pair, Mr and AQA 3.3.9 / OCR A module 6.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed. Kid paragraphs each carry one idea (the C=O dipole, dipole–dipole forces with numbers, the hydrogen bond limit, solubility and chain length). Adult paragraphs give the specification context, the mechanism with data, five named mistakes and the lab outline. Overlap with Aldehydes, ketones and the carbonyl group and Intermolecular forces stays under the 12% gate.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots for all six steps: ladder rungs and force tiles span the width with 14 px text, the propanone and water molecules sit apart with readable δ labels, chain bars have a colour legend drawn as swatches and the 100 °C label clear of the C6 bar, and thermometer marks sit above the scale so every tick label shows.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, and all five Show me tasks completed. Every canvas tap or drag has a labelled button twin ('To a lone pair on the C=O oxygen', 'Put ethanal at 20 °C', 'Add a carbon') and the canvas aria-label speaks each result, such as 'ethanal: boils at 20 °C, very soluble'.
